Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers to learn complex patterns from large amounts of data, enabling tasks like image recognition and natural language processing.
NLP stands for Natural Language Processing, a field of AI.
Transformers are a type of neural network architecture that uses self-attention mechanisms to process sequential data in parallel.
Convolutional Neural Networks are specialized for processing grid-like data such as images.
Python is a high-level programming language known for its readability.
Recurrent Neural Networks process sequential data by maintaining hidden states.
TensorFlow is an open-source ML framework developed by Google.
PyTorch is a deep learning framework known for its dynamic computation graphs.
A loss function measures how well a model's predictions match the expected output.
An epoch is one complete pass through the entire training dataset.
Batch size is the number of training examples used in one iteration.
Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training to prevent overfitting.
Regularization techniques prevent overfitting by adding penalties to model complexity.
Learning rate controls how much model weights are updated during training.
Stochastic Gradient Descent updates weights using random subsets of data.
Adam combines momentum and adaptive learning rates for efficient optimization.
Cross-validation evaluates model performance by splitting data into multiple folds.
Precision is the ratio of true positives to all predicted positives.
Recall is the ratio of true positives to all actual positives.
F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
AUC represents the area under the ROC curve, measuring classifier performance.
